verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_fibonacci_polyglot: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The core logic uses single-letter names: `a`, `b`, `t`, `k`, `n`, `s`. The polyglot switch lines `""" //"` / `""" #"` have no comment in the file explaining the trick. There is one useful comment on the bignum layout.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `main` is short, but the generated binary `polyglot/cmain` was committed in the diff. `#include <string.h>` is never used. All the C logic is crammed into `main`, with no fib helper.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: There is no input validation. `atol(argv[1])` turns non-numeric input into 0. Negative input gives `(size_t)(n * 0.21)`, which is undefined behaviour. `calloc`/`malloc` results are not checked and the memory is never freed. `0.21` is a magic constant. Python only handles a missing argument by crashing with a traceback.

items.name: Boundary and large inputs
items.evidence: f(0), f(1) and large n match in both languages; bignum C was tested up to 500. Argument errors are not handled: C prints 0 for `abc` or `-5`, and Python crashes with a traceback when the argument is missing.

items.name: Exact invocation contract
items.evidence: It works with the exact commands and compiles cleanly under -Wall -Wextra. But the agent left the extra artifact `polyglot/cmain` in /app/polyglot, which plausibly caused the hidden test failure: the directory isn't left holding only main.py.c.
